description: ANSI/TIA-222 is the United States standard for the structural design, analysis, modification, maintenance and condition assessment of antenna supporting structures: guyed masts, self-supporting lattice towers and monopoles that carry broadcast, mobile and microwave antennas. First issued in 1959 and maintained by the TIA TR-14 committee, it sets design loads for wind, ice and earthquakes, rules for analysing existing structures when antennas are added, and a maintenance section with recommended inspection intervals: every three years for guyed masts and every five years for self-supporting structures, and after severe weather, with shorter intervals in coastal and corrosive settings. Revision H dated from 2017; a revision period opened in May 2022 considered drone inspections and the loads of 5G deployments, and Revision I took effect on 1 January 2024. The Telecommunications Industry Foundation offers a free guide to the maintenance and condition assessment provisions, with checklists, field mapping tools and guy tension and plumb charts from the standard's annex. Coverage: United States practice, also used in other countries. Format and access: the standard is sold through TIA's standards store; the TIF guide is a free PDF. Caveats: the standard is paid and copyrighted; it contains no inventory of towers or their condition; revision I details were not read. Simulation uses: fragility of towers and masts under wind and ice, inspection and ageing assumptions for asset condition models, and loads for adding antennas. Related records: the CRREL icing and tower failure study and the broadcast mast collapse list give failure evidence.
